identity.name: Datograph Up/Down
identity.one_liner: The 2012 update to the original 1999 Datograph, adding a power-reserve display to the flyback chronograph movement collectors already rated among the finest column-wheel calibers made.

provenance_events.description: The Datograph debuts at Basel 1999 with the calibre L951.1 — the first in-house chronograph from A. Lange & Söhne, and a movement that defines the next two decades of chronograph collecting. The "Up/Down" power-reserve version follows in 2012.

narrative.story: The original 1999 Datograph put Lange's in-house L951.1 column-wheel flyback chronograph on the map, hand-finished to a standard most chronograph houses reserved for time-only movements. The Up/Down update shown here, introduced at SIHH 2012, adds a power-reserve indicator alongside the running minute counter, giving the L951.6 a longer 60-hour reserve without changing the case proportions that made the original legible and symmetrical.
narrative.collector_notes: Collectors check the jumping minute counter for a clean, instantaneous snap rather than a lagging creep, since the snail cam that drives it is a known service point. The black dial with white gold in this reference reads flatter under bright light than the silver dial versions; both are original factory options, not a later swap.
